items.title: Dozens of countries agree to 'largest ever' oil stocks release
items.description: The International Energy Agency agrees to release 400 million barrels of oil, the largest such move in its history.

items.title: Live: Trump says he is not worried about Iran-backed attack in US
items.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation reportedly warns police departments in California that Iran could retaliate to US attacks by launching drones at the US West Coast. Follow live.

items.title: As war rages, this small island is vital to the Iranian regime and its enemies
items.description: There is a small island in the Persian Gulf that is vital to the flow of Iranian oil to its customers and, analysts say, if Washington or Israel were to seize it the regime's war chest would soon dry up.

items.title: Matt Canavan can tackle One Nation but Coalition's problems run deeper
items.description: Matt Canavan's rise to the Nationals leadership gives the Coalition a fighter capable of taking on Pauline Hanson, but beating back One Nation is only part of the opposition's electoral dilemma.

items.title: War, oil, inflation are all creating interest rate perfect storm
items.description: Expectations the Reserve Bank will hike the cash rate next week are rising as leading economists shift their forecasts — and some say one increase may not be enough.

items.title: How to reclaim the classroom from the rising 'manosphere'
items.description: Teachers say misogynistic behaviour from young, male students has been getting worse. A guide has been released to help teachers, schools and young people recognise the manosphere's impacts and access tools to reclaim the classroom.

items.title: Former spy boss resigns from antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Dennis Richardson was originally tapped by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in the weeks after the Bondi terror attack to lead a review into the federal government's intelligence and security agencies.

items.title: Magnitude-4.4 earthquake shakes regional NSW
items.description: Thousands of people report feeling a magnitude-4.4 earthquake that has hit Boorowa in southern New South Wales.

items.title: Two people arrested less than a week after hate speech laws pass parliament
items.description: Police say a man has been charged and a woman is assisting them with inquiries over the use of phrases deemed antisemitic by the Queensland government.

items.title: Allan government plans to make vendors fund building and pest reports
items.description: The Victorian government says it will make home sellers pay for building and pest inspections rather than home buyers if it wins this year's state election in November.

items.title: Iconic Australian-made pinball machines preserved for generations to come
items.description: Five pinball machines, including the first licensed Star Wars unit, have been saved from the scrap heap and will eventually be made available for the public to play at a special exhibition.

items.title: More pain to come after Qantas hikes international airfares
items.description: As Qantas hikes international airfares due to a surge in fuel prices from the Middle East war, an industry expert warns it's only the start of what's to come.

items.title: More views of SA Liberal candidate emerge against Islam and 'trans agenda'
items.description: More views by Liberal Party candidate and evangelical Christian Carston Woodhouse emerge with the Adelaide man saying Islam is "poisonous and wrong" and the "trans agenda is insanity". Warning: This story contains content some readers might find distressing.

items.title: Booming gold explorers are buying up wineries
items.description: As the wine industry struggles with increased challenges, some Victorian wineries are choosing to sell their land to mining companies.

items.title: Chance find reunites former cop with the protester he arrested
items.description: Ian Wright captured the Franklin River blockade on film. Forty years later, the officer who arrested him reached out.

items.title: A six-year-old’s terrified phone call is the foundation of The Voice of Hind Rajab
items.description: Protests erupted following the killing of six-year-old Hind Rajab at the hands of Israeli forces. Two years later, her story is in the running for an Academy Award.

items.title: Government doubles graduate visa fee but some countries exempt
items.description: Tiered pricing for visas is being used to support Pacific nations but some fear it could be misused to target certain communities.

items.title: Man arrested, teen on the run after alleged four-day crime spree
items.description: A Mildura man has been remanded in custody and his accomplice remains on the run after the pair allegedly went on a four-day crime spree across Victoria.

items.title: Main link between Sydney and western NSW to be closed for weeks
items.description: A crucial bridge on the Great Western Highway linking Sydney to the state's Central West will be shut for at least a fortnight, while specialists assess why it is moving and cracking.

items.title: Summer rivalry fuelling new Aussie para-winter star
items.description: Lauren Parker has finished eighth in the women's 10km sitting para cross-country skiing at the Milano Cortina Games, just nine months after taking up the sport.

items.title: NT government knocks back move to scrutinise bullying claims against MLA
items.description: A Northern Territory government backbencher accused of bullying has faced a bid for a parliamentary inquiry into his alleged conduct, as well as an extraordinary berating from the NT Speaker.

items.title: WOMADelaide 2026 was pure joy — here’s what went down
items.description: At Adelaide's global music weekender, tens of thousands transform everyday anxieties into a shared burst of joy.

items.title: Triple killer lived with two foster children, minister lashes department
items.description: NSW Minister for Families and Communities Kate Washington says the mistake is the worst she has seen in her time in the portfolio.

items.title: What happens when online NAPLAN testing is disrupted?
items.description: Technical difficulties delayed NAPLAN testing across the country today. Here's how to navigate disruptions and what it means for your child.

items.title: Former inspector tells CFMEU inquiry she felt pressured to issue $3,600 fine
items.description: A Workplace Health and Safety Queensland told the inquiry she believed the regulator had formed an "alliance" with the CFMEU.
